article.headline: A Claude Code Skill That Mines the Social Web for Working Prompts
article.lede: A new open-source skill for Claude Code sweeps a dozen social platforms for the last month of community discussion on any topic, then generates a ready-to-use prompt based on what practitioners are actually finding effective right now. It was built by Matt Van Horn, a serial entrepreneur who co-founded Lyft and later sold a smart-oven startup to Weber. The tool has accumulated more than 25,000 GitHub stars since its January 2026 launch.
article.body:
A Claude Code *skill* called `/last30days` does something deceptively simple: you type a topic, and it queries a dozen social platforms and aggregators for the past thirty days of discussion, then synthesises what it finds into a single, citation-backed brief — complete with a ready-to-use **prompt** built from patterns the community is actively upvoting. The result lands in your editor within seconds. The skill is free, MIT-licensed, and installs in Claude Code with a single slash command.

The author is Matt Van Horn, a serial entrepreneur best known for co-founding Zimride, the carpooling service that evolved into **Lyft (LYFT)**, and for building the June Intelligent Oven, a countertop appliance that used computer vision to identify food and cook it automatically; Weber, the grill manufacturer, acquired June Life in a reported nine-figure deal. Van Horn's current project is, by comparison, decidedly scrappier: a 25,000-star GitHub repository written almost entirely in Python.

The skill's architecture is more intricate than a simple search. Under the hood it queries Reddit via *ScrapeCreators* (a third-party scraping API), X, Bluesky's *AT Protocol*, YouTube — pulling transcripts via the open-source tool *yt-dlp* — TikTok, Instagram, Hacker News, *Polymarket* (a prediction-market platform), and the broader web through Brave Software's search API. Each result is scored on a weighted formula that privileges engagement and comment depth; top-comment signals carry an additional boost. The synthesised output is automatically saved as a Markdown file, building what the README calls a “personal research library.”

Distribution runs through Claude Code’s third-party *plugin marketplace* system — a relatively new facility that lets developers publish skills, agents, and hooks via any GitHub repository, much as an app store lets developers distribute software. A separate directory called *ClawHub*, associated with an AI agent framework called OpenClaw, also lists the skill; the two install commands visible in the screenshot above target different hosts. The tool has drawn crossover interest because the underlying problem — *prompt decay*, the tendency for specific techniques to stop working as AI models are retrained or updated — is acutely felt across every major tool category.

The “feels like cheating” framing in the post is understandable but worth testing. The skill synthesises what communities *say* is working, which is not the same as independently verified evidence. Community upvotes are a signal, not a proof; viral prompt patterns can be cargo-culted as easily as they can be tested. The real value is closer to what a good research assistant provides: it saves hours of thread-diving and surfaces patterns a busy practitioner might otherwise miss. Whether those patterns hold depends, as always, on the work that follows.

concepts.definition: A plugin for Anthropic’s Claude Code CLI tool that adds new slash commands, agents, or hooks. Skills are distributed via GitHub repositories and installed through Claude Code’s built-in plugin marketplace system.
The open, federated networking protocol that underpins Bluesky. It allows users to move their accounts and data between servers — unlike Twitter/X, where accounts are locked to the platform.

A third-party API service that provides programmatic access to content from Reddit, TikTok, Instagram, and other social platforms that restrict direct scraping. One API key covers multiple platforms simultaneously.

An open-source command-line tool for downloading video and audio from YouTube and hundreds of other sites. The last30days skill uses it to extract video transcripts for analysis alongside social posts.

A decentralised prediction-market platform where users stake real money on the outcomes of future events. The skill includes it as a source because market odds can reflect informed community consensus about what is likely to happen.

Claude Code’s system for distributing third-party extensions. Developers publish a GitHub repository in a specific format; users register it with a slash command and then install individual skills from its catalog.

The tendency for specific AI prompt techniques to stop working as models are retrained or updated. A prompt that reliably elicits a certain output today may produce different or worse results after the next model update.
An AI agent framework with its own plugin ecosystem and marketplace (ClawHub). Distinct from Claude Code, though some tools — including last30days — publish install packages to both platforms.

repos.summary: The canonical open-source repository for the last30days Claude Code skill. Written primarily in Python, it orchestrates searches across 13-plus social platforms and web sources, scores results by engagement, and synthesises findings into a Markdown brief with a ready-to-use prompt. MIT-licensed, with more than 25,000 GitHub stars as of May 2026 after growing from 1,500 at launch in January 2026.

article.fact_check: The tweet presents the author as anonymous (“someone built”), but the tool is publicly attributed to Matt Van Horn (GitHub: mvanhorn), a well-documented entrepreneur. The post also summarises the source list as “Reddit and X,” though the skill actually queries more than a dozen platforms including Bluesky, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Hacker News, and Polymarket. Both are simplifications rather than errors. The version shown (v2.9.5) was current at posting; by the time of this brief the tool had reached v3.1.1 with a substantially expanded feature set, including a ground-up architecture rewrite.

ticker_lyft.blurb: Lyft, Inc. operates a peer-to-peer ridesharing platform in the United States and Canada, connecting drivers with passengers via a mobile app. The company also offers bikes, scooters, and transit partnerships. As the second-largest ridesharing company in the U.S., Lyft competes primarily with Uber and has been focusing on profitability and autonomous vehicle partnerships.
ticker_lyft.recent: In the past 30 days, Lyft reported better-than-expected Q4 2024 earnings, with revenue growing 15% year-over-year and the company achieving its first full-year positive free cash flow. The stock rose on the news, but remains volatile amid competition and regulatory concerns. Analysts have mixed ratings, with some citing improved margins and others cautious on growth.
